t.2.107.1: Then, having settled his mothers in Ayodhyā, Bharata, firm in his vow and burning with grief, spoke these words to his elders.
t.2.107.2: I shall go to Nandigrāma; today I take leave of you all. There, without Rāghava, I shall endure all this sorrow.
t.2.107.3: For the king has gone to heaven, and my elder dwells in the forest; I await Rāma for the kingship, for he is the king of great renown.
t.2.107.4: Having heard these auspicious words of the great-souled Bharata, all the ministers and Vasiṣṭha, the family priest, spoke.
t.2.107.5: O Bharata, the words you have spoken out of affection for your brother are fitting and praiseworthy; they are worthy of you alone.
t.2.107.6: What man would not approve of you, who are ever devoted to your kinsmen, who stand firm in brotherly affection, and who have taken the path of the noble?
t.2.107.7: Having heard the pleasing words of the ministers, just as he had wished, he spoke these words to the charioteer: "Let my chariot be yoked."
t.2.107.8: With a joyful face, the glorious one, having respectfully saluted all the mothers, mounted the chariot, accompanied by Śatrughna.
t.2.107.9: Having quickly mounted the chariot, both Śatrughna and Bharata, supremely delighted, set forth, surrounded by ministers and family priests.
t.2.107.10: There, in front, went the venerable elders, the twice-born led by Vasiṣṭha, all facing east, toward where Nandigrāma lay.
t.2.107.11: When Bharata had set out, that army too, crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, marched forth unsummoned, and so did all the inhabitants of the city.
t.2.107.12: Then righteous Bharata, devoted to his brother, seated in his chariot, went swiftly to Nandigrāma, having placed the pair of sandals upon his head.
t.2.107.13: Then Bharata, having swiftly entered Nandigrāma, quickly descended from his chariot and spoke these words to his elders.
t.2.107.14: This kingdom has been given to me by my brother himself as a trust, and with it these gold-adorned sandals that ensure its welfare and security. I shall protect it until Rāghava's return.
t.2.107.15: Quickly fitting them once more upon Rāghava with my own hands, I shall behold those feet of Rāma together with the sandals.
t.2.107.16: Then, having laid down my burden and being reunited with Rāghava, I shall hand over the kingdom to my elder and take up the conduct befitting one who serves his elder.
t.2.107.18: But once Kākutstha has been consecrated and the people are thrilled and joyful, my delight and my glory as well would be fourfold greater than from the kingship itself.
t.2.107.17: Having handed over to Rāghava the deposit entrusted to me, these excellent sandals, together with this kingdom and Ayodhyā, I shall be cleansed of sin.
t.2.107.19: Lamenting thus, the wretched and illustrious Bharata, grief-stricken, ruled the kingdom from Nandigrāma together with his ministers.
t.2.107.20: Then that heroic lord Bharata, wearing bark garments and matted locks and bearing the guise of a sage, dwelt in Nandigrāma together with his army.
t.2.107.21: Then Bharata, devoted to his brother, longing for Rāma's return, obedient to his brother's word and determined to see his vow through to the end.
t.2.107.22: Then, having consecrated the two sandals, Bharata dwelt at that time in Nandigrāma, and he reported all matters of governance to the sandals.
